entries.claim: The rotation admission check reserves only the pending record, not the mandatory rotation-marker line written into the fresh record.
entries.failure_scenario: Create a small existing reads file and submit a serializable record whose rendered line is just below `MAX_READS_BYTES` (for example `MAX_READS_BYTES - 1` bytes). `size + pending >= MAX_READS_BYTES` triggers rotation and the `pending >= MAX_READS_BYTES` rejection does not apply. `rotateReads` then writes the marker into the fresh file, after which `appendFileSync` appends the nearly-max-sized line without another capacity check. The resulting live `reads.jsonl` is larger than 8 MiB, violating the stated size cap.

entries.claim: After only 250 ms waiting on an in-flight claim, a losing writer returns success-path control to `appendRead` even if the winner still has not swapped the live path.
entries.failure_scenario: A rotator successfully hard-links the full live record, then is descheduled/SIGSTOPed for more than 250 ms before `renameSync(temp, file)`. Each concurrent appender at the bound waits until this loop expires, returns `{rotated:false}`, and reaches the unconditional append at line 777. Because the pathname still names the old inode, all of those writes accumulate in the claimed old generation. A sufficiently busy process set can grow that generation arbitrarily past 8 MiB before the winner resumes and makes it `reads.1.jsonl`; if the winner is then killed, appenders continue taking this path until the 30-second stale timeout. Thus concurrent appenders can defeat the cap during an otherwise live rotation.

counter_evidence.note: The losing writer appending into the pre-swap inode is the documented posture at this site, not a defect: the comment states it reports rotated:false "so the caller appends into whatever the winner left", and PLAN-1 requires only that concurrent appenders leave every record present somewhere across the pair, which this satisfies since that inode becomes reads.1.jsonl. The arbitrary-growth escalation is contradicted by READS_CLAIM_STALE_MS at line 367 with the wasStale reclaim arm at line 590: a winner stopped past 30s has its claim reclaimed and the rotation completes, so the old generation cannot grow without bound.
